newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Astra, Comercial kick off bolsa trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Astra, Comercial kick off bolsa trade.

text.p: Oil concern Astra and holding firm Comercial del Plata got trade off to an early start on the Argentine bolsa Friday on news of big corporate deals, brokers said.
Astra and Comercial del Plata rose 1.0 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively, pushing the blue-chip MerVal index up 0.1 percent to 768.01.

Spain's Repsol said Friday it would buy stakes in local firms through its subsidiary Astra for $345 million, while Comercial del Plata said it would raise $330 million from deals to sell interests in several Argentine companies.

"We're seeing huge foreign interest in Argentine banks and companies, and while this may not be reflected in bolsa volume and prices yet, it's creating a very bullish long-term scenario," said Leonardo Torres Barsanti at Rio Research.

HSBC Holdings said Friday it was buying out the local financial services group Roberts, while Spain's Santander said Tuesday it was acquiring a controlling stake in Banco Rio de la Plata. Two weeks earlier, Banco Frances announced the purchase of Banco de Credito Argentino.
"Market sentiment will be very good today and we're bucking the weaker trend on Wall Street," another trader said.

"Moreover (oil giant) YPF looks ready to recover today because with current levels of demand, the secondary stock offering it announced yesterday should go very smoothly -- maybe the whole lump will be sold a single corporate investor," the trader said.
YPF closed off 1.7 percent Thursday after it announced plans to float the 10 percent stake assigned for purchase by employees when the company was privatized in 1993.
Analysts said the MerVal was near resistance levels but individual stocks affected by business deals, like banks, Astra and Comercial del Plata, would rise selectively.

"The MerVal is likely to stay rangebound in the short term but some stocks have a lot more growth potential," Barsanti said. "In the long term, it looks like Argentina may be on the road to full development and low financial risk because of the foreign capital that is arriving -- on the banking side we're seeing growing concentration and on the business side we've got a rush of foreign investment."
